matches.gold_text: Proposals must be emailed to the Research Director at MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 10 a.m. Central on the due date, August 21, 2024, according to the email time stamp.
The submittal must include a project plan, the proposed project team and its background, and any related projects now active or recently completed by the firm.
Questions and comments about the RFP must be sent to the Research Director by email by the deadline of 7/17/2024, 4 p.m. Central.
The proposal must include all data required in the Required Elements of Proposal section, or it may be disqualified.
The proposal should reference the project number and title, since more than one RFP may be due at the same time.
The Work Plan section of the proposal should be no longer than ten pages and use a font size of at least 12 points, excluding forms and resumes.
The project plan must include all items outlined in Section 2 (Scope of Work).
The project plan must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve the work plans.
Proposals must include a work plan with a proposed timeline.
The Personnel section should give the name, location, telephone number and email address of the Offeror's primary contact person.
The Offeror must provide a complete listing of each sub-offeror, if any, with complete contact information.
The proposal must clearly identify the Offeror's experience in offering the requested services during the past three years.
Proposals should give the name, title and telephone number of at least three client officials from within the past three years as references.
The proposal must be submitted as a single combined PDF document.

The proposal must contain only the required documents, in this order: Proposal Submission Form, Cover Letter, Body of Proposal (including work plan and project schedule), Personnel, Organization's Project Experience, Team Member Experience, and Organization's Client References.
A cover letter is optional and, if included, must not exceed one page.
The Offeror must submit a proposed cost estimate covering all services defined in the Scope of Work.
The cost estimate must be shown on the Section (4) Price Page, which must be completed, signed and returned with the proposal.
The services must be provided for a price not exceeding $175,000.
The contract period will be 15 months.
The Offeror must submit quarterly updates on work accomplished on or before the last working day of March, June, September and December throughout the project.
The quarterly updates must be submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager.
An interim presentation to update MoDOT on progress must be completed by 9/15/2025.
The Offeror must provide ongoing progress updates by email and phone to MoDOT contacts every month.
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025.
The final report, summary report, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026, about one month before the contract ends.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends on 2/2/2026.
The Offeror must facilitate a kick-off meeting with MoDOT to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to establish a protocol for regular communications and coordination.
The Offeror must schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings reviewing past progress and upcoming work, in person or online.
The Offeror must develop minutes for the kick-off meeting and each quarterly status meeting.
The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT within two weeks after the project kick-off meeting.
The Data Management Plan should address use of platform-independent, non-proprietary data formats to maximize future utility of the data.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
Before work begins on the proof of concept, the Offeror must provide the name of the program used to develop the legal land descriptions.
MoDOT Information Systems must approve the program before the Offeror proceeds to Task 3c (proof of concept).
The Offeror must demonstrate that the technology can create draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties.
The Offeror must provide training to MoDOT right-of-way staff once the system is developed and finalized.
The training must come with a user manual for staff to reference.
The Offeror must prepare a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with all accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study.
The draft documents should be final products apart from revisions based on MoDOT's review.
The final report must include a completed Technical Report Documentation page.
The Offeror must develop a final report detailing the tasks completed and all findings from the project.
The Offeror must provide a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions.
The Offeror must provide a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing important details of the project.
Property descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide.
Property rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method unless the property is acquired in its entirety.
When a property is acquired in its entirety, the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Offerors are encouraged to obtain 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation.
All documents and reports produced by the Offeror at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC's property.
MHTC may reproduce and use any products derived from the Offeror's work without paying royalties or fees.

The Offeror should be able to provide a Missouri workers' compensation policy or equivalent as required by state law.

Web applications must use the MVC, Razor Pages or Web API framework.

checklist.fact: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), coordinated by the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, for MoDOT as the beneficiary (Right of Way staff are the users of the tool).
The need: property descriptions for MHTC must be written by metes and bounds and reviewed by a professional land surveyor, and these descriptions are long and tedious to write.
The project goal is to determine the usefulness of AI and ML to develop a "first draft" legal land description using MHTC parameters, which MoDOT Right of Way staff would review and edit.
The services are capped at a not-to-exceed price of $175,000.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project assumed to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending February 2, 2026 with the final invoice due.
Proposals for project TR202504 must be emailed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.
Questions must be submitted by 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central via the RFP email only; contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification.
Property descriptions must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, which the RFP references but does not include.

Core deliverables include a data management plan, a proof-of-concept demonstration of AI writing legal land descriptions, training and a user manual for ROW staff, and draft and final reports; the final report, summary, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026.
The Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.
Web applications must meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility conformance.
No PII may be stored in any database table unless there is a specific business need, and any stored PII requires approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.

specificity.reason: Most components name concrete deliverables, dates, roles and technologies; the AI/ML method itself (model choice, evaluation metrics, parameter set) stays fairly generic.

feasibility.reason: Plausible, but MoDOT IS approval of the development program before 4/25/2025 is a risky dependency, the DMP date is assumed to be satisfied, and a full app plus training fits $175k only loosely.

consistency.reason: Technology, accessibility, budget and dates are respected, but the DMP is set to 12/4/2024, past the 2-weeks-after-kick-off deadline, and the 15-month term is reinterpreted to fit the fixed dates.

component_records.title: Qualified research organization and study mobilisation
component_records.description: The bidder is a qualified research organization that will conduct the TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions" study for MHTC and MoDOT, and it demonstrates that qualification through its past-three-years experience delivering AI/ML and right-of-way research services, its named principal investigator and land-surveying subject-matter expert, and its three client references. Mobilisation starts at award: we confirm the project number and title, stand up the project management and document-control structure, and prepare for the 11/15/2024 kick-off. All questions and requests for information about the RFP are submitted only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov and no later than 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, with no contact with MoDOT employees by any other method, so the bid remains responsive.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: We run the study under a single project manager who is the named point of contact for the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, and who fully coordinates all activities with that division and keeps advice and information on Agreement matters available to it as the work progresses. A kick-off meeting with MoDOT reviews the work plan, scope and schedule and establishes the protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination, and we minute that meeting and every quarterly status meeting. The finalized work plan details implementation of each project task with the resources and schedule required, and is expressly subject to MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. We provide monthly e-mail and phone updates to MoDOT contacts in addition to the quarterly cycle, and we consult MHTC's representative on any concern arising in the administration of the services. All RFP events we host or attend are scheduled between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central, and we meet every submission deadline in the RFP on the basis that time is of the essence.

component_records.title: Schedule, milestones and deliverable control
component_records.description: We manage the study against a milestone baseline that fixes the data management plan, the MoDOT-supplied example LLDs, the AI/ML drafting demonstration, training and manual delivery, the interim presentation, the draft final report and the final report, and we report progress against it at every status meeting. The baseline holds the data management plan to 12/4/2024, the interim presentation to 9/15/2025, the draft final report, summary report and user manual to 11/3/2025, the final report, summary report, presentation and user manual to 1/1/2026, and the final invoice and contract end to 2/2/2026, with the 15-month contract period as the outer bound. Because the final deliverables land a month before contract end, all billing is completed before the final invoice. We treat the RFP's dates as firm and raise any proposed change through a formal contract amendment rather than by informal slippage.

component_records.title: Data management plan and research data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks of kick-off we submit a Data Management Plan to MoDOT that describes the anticipated formats of the project's data and related files, and that commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the example LLDs, extracted parameters, training data and evaluation results retain maximum future utility for MoDOT. The plan also sets out how MoDOT-supplied example descriptions are stored, versioned and access-controlled, and how confidential factual matters supplied by MHTC are held, marked and kept from third-party disclosure except as statute, ordinance, court order or MHTC's representative authorises, with immediate notification to MHTC of any request for such information. No PII is stored in any project database table without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.

component_records.title: Literature review of state DOT AI/ML practice in right of way
component_records.description: We conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOTs' use of AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering published research, DOT technical reports, vendor and pilot documentation and peer state practice, and we deliver it as an annotated review with a synthesis of what is transferable to MoDOT's LLD workflow. The review is scoped to the ROW use cases that bear on drafting legal descriptions, and it feeds directly into the design choices for the proof of concept so that the demonstration is grounded in documented practice rather than vendor claims. Findings are reported to the Construction and Materials Division as the work progresses and carried into the final report.

component_records.title: LLD requirements baseline and program approval
component_records.description: Before any drafting work we build a requirements baseline that encodes MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 and the RFP's description rules: metes and bounds for every realty right acquired or conveyed unless the property is taken in its entirety, in which case the description is written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record, and explicit recital of the specific rights acquired, conveyed or leased where less than fee simple title is conveyed, accurately described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4-1/4 calls. We name the program used to develop the LLDs and submit it with the supporting information MoDOT Information Systems needs, and we do not proceed to the Task 3c proof of concept until MoDOT Information Systems has approved it. The baseline doubles as the acceptance checklist against which ROW staff judge every AI-drafted description.

component_records.title: AI/ML drafting engine and proof of concept
component_records.description: We build the AI/ML capability that produces a first draft legal land description from MHTC parameters, and we demonstrate it live on a variety of properties so MoDOT can review the drafts and give feedback on improvements. The demonstration is the RFP's proof-of-concept test: it shows the technology creating draft LLDs across differing property types, with each draft scored against the requirements baseline and the gaps fed back into the model and prompt design. The application is web-based and needs no client-side software beyond a modern browser, is built on .NET 6.0 or above with MVC, Razor Pages or Web API in C#, JavaScript, CSS and HTML, uses Python only for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the BRPT approves larger use, and runs any on-premise database on Oracle 19C. It meets WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, is tested on the latest IS-approved browsers, carries no third-party tooling that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without BRPT and IS management approval, uses no unlicensed third-party content, and shows no vendor branding where a licensed option exists to remove it. Library dependencies are reviewed and updated annually.

component_records.title: Training, user manual and ROW staff enablement
component_records.description: Once the tool is developed and finalised we train ROW staff on how to use it, delivering instructor-led sessions plus recorded walkthroughs so staff who cannot attend live are still covered, and we hand over a standalone user manual that documents the workflow from MHTC parameters to reviewed draft description, the review and edit steps, and the EPG 236.4.6.2 checks the tool performs. The manual is a maintained deliverable, updated after the demonstration feedback and reissued with the draft and final report packages, so the version staff hold matches the version in service. Training and the manual are delivered on 7/25/2025 and refreshed in the 11/3/2025 and 1/1/2026 deliverable sets.

component_records.title: Reporting, research summary and presentation
component_records.description: We produce a final report detailing every task completed and all findings generated during the project, a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff summarising the significant details of the project. The interim presentation is delivered by 9/15/2025 and the draft final report, summary report and user manual by 11/3/2025, with the final set due 1/1/2026 so billing closes before the 2/2/2026 contract end. Reports and summaries follow the RFP's Publications Guidelines and summary template, and the final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page. All deliverables are produced at MHTC's direction and remain MHTC property, with MHTC free to reproduce and use derived products without royalty.

component_records.title: Contracts, compliance and insurance obligations
component_records.description: We accept the RFP's contract provisions as they will appear in the post-award negotiated contract, and we accept that MHTC may cancel the award and select another Offeror if terms cannot be agreed. We acknowledge that the Agreement comprises the RFP and its written amendments, our proposal and the signed post-award contract, that written clarifications issued by MHTC govern over conflicting requirements, and that any change requires a formal contract amendment signed by both authorised representatives. We do not release any material or report to the public without MHTC's representative's prior consent, do not assign, delegate or novate any interest without prior written consent, and remain fully responsible to MHTC for the quality and performance of all services including those of subcontractors and suppliers. We flow Section (3), paragraph I of the Agreement into every subcontract and take any action the Commission directs to enforce those provisions, including sanctions for noncompliance. We certify that every assigned employee is eligible and authorised to work in the United States, provide the completed E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding for proposed staff, and submit the sworn affidavit that we do not knowingly employ unauthorised aliens. We keep all working papers available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at no charge during the Agreement and for three years after final payment. We carry General Liability and Automobile Liability at not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent, and can furnish certificates before contract signing.

items.text: The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) on behalf of the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing draft property descriptions.
The project is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and the Offeror must fully coordinate its activities with that division.

MoDOT must describe every realty right it acquires or conveys by metes and bounds unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2 and must recite specific rights when less than fee simple title is conveyed.

Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to a grantor, a professional land surveyor must verify that the description matches the right of way plans and that the plans match the surveyor's field data.
Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the RFP.
MoDOT's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, and quarterly project updates feed the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA.

MoDOT's Information Systems group, including its Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management, must approve the technology stack, so the client already operates under a defined enterprise IT standards regime.

MoDOT wants research to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for producing a "first draft" legal land description (LLD) from MHTC parameters that Right of Way staff can then review and edit.

The work is procured as a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," and Offerors are invited to propose the best strategies for accomplishing the research objectives rather than simply execute fixed task descriptions.

The scope comprises six tasks: project management, a literature review of other state DOTs' AI/ML use for right-of-way purposes, a proof of concept (including MoDOT-supplied example LLDs, program approval, and a demonstration of AI drafting LLDs), training and a user manual, a draft report and research summary, and a final report, research summary and presentation.
The contract period is 15 months, with an estimated start of November 1, 2024, a final report due 1/1/2026 and the contract ending with the final invoice on 2/2/2026.

Key milestones include a kick-off meeting on 11/15/2024, a data management plan due 12/4/2024, MoDOT supplying approved LLD examples on 12/20/2024, an AI/ML drafting demonstration on 4/25/2025, training and manual delivery on 7/25/2025, an interim presentation on 9/15/2025, and a draft final report on 11/3/2025.
The Offeror must deliver a 1-2 page research summary stating project objectives, findings and conclusions, plus a presentation for MoDOT staff summarizing significant project details.
The Offeror must provide training to ROW staff on how to use the finalized tool, supported by a user manual.
Proposals are due by email to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.

All questions and requests for information must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, and contacting MoDOT employees by any other method is cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its public responses to questions on 7/31/2024 and notifies submitters of project selection or interviews on 9/18/2024.

The award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, evaluated after a responsiveness determination against criteria set by the Technical Advisory Committee, whose specific criteria and weights are not stated in the RFP.
The proof of concept is judged through a live demonstration of the technology creating draft LLDs on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving feedback on improvements.

The Work Plan must be narrative, no more than ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, must cover all items in Section 2, and must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.

Proposals must be submitted as one combined PDF in a fixed order: Proposal Submission Form, optional one-page cover letter, body of proposal (work plan and schedule), personnel, organization's project experience, team member experience, and organization's client references.
Proposals must identify experience delivering the requested services in the past three years and list at least three client references with name, title and telephone number from the past three years.
Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, with costs itemized on the Section (4) Price Page across salaries, benefits, operating expense, F&A, and miscellaneous.

Any application must be built on approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or supported .NET Framework 4.8+), MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, and only C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python reserved for ESRI scripts and other small one-time uses unless the BRPT approves larger use.

Applications must be web-based, require no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets or Silverlight), and meet WCAG 2.1 level AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508.

On-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server (SQL Server 2016+ only with MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval), and no PII may be stored without a specific business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.
The Offeror must name the program used to develop the LLDs and obtain MoDOT Information Systems approval before proceeding to the Task 3c proof of concept.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain the property of MHTC, and MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties.
The Offeror must keep all working papers available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at no charge during the agreement and for three (3) years after final payment.

The RFP refers to documents the bidder must obtain separately: the Proposal Submission Form, the Standard Research Agreement, the Publication Guidelines and summary template, the cost estimate template, and the Exhibit A (E-Verify) and Exhibit B (lawful presence) affidavits, none of which are included in the RFP text.
The RFP is issued by the Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission on behalf of MoDOT, and the work is procured as research study TR202504. (S8.1, S9.1)
All questions and requests for information must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central. (S12.1, S33.1)
The project is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, with which the Offeror must fully coordinate. (S1.1, S49.1)

The RFP fixes a 11/15/2024 kick-off, a 12/4/2024 data management plan, a 4/25/2025 demonstration, 7/25/2025 training, a 9/15/2025 interim presentation, an 11/3/2025 draft final report, a 1/1/2026 final report and a 2/2/2026 contract end. (S15.2)
MoDOT supplies approved example LLDs on 12/20/2024 for use in the proof of concept. (S15.2)
Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 and recite specific rights when less than fee simple title is conveyed. (S9.1)
MoDOT's Information Systems group, including its Best Practices Review Team and IS management, must approve the technology stack. (S73.1, S22.1)
Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, itemised on the Section (4) Price Page. (S17.1, S47.1)

The RFP's fixed milestone dates are treated as firm and are not renegotiated at kick-off, so the kick-off meeting confirms the coordination protocol and resourcing rather than resetting the schedule. (S15.2, S19.1)
The data management plan is delivered on 12/4/2024, which is treated as satisfying the two-weeks-after-kick-off deadline because the kick-off is 11/15/2024. (S15.2, S19.1)
The 15-month contract period is read as running from the 11/15/2024 kick-off to the 2/2/2026 contract end, with the RFP's fixed dates governing over the stated term. (S11.1, S15.2)
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are delivered on 11/3/2025, the fixed table date, rather than the approximate two-months-before-final-report date. (S15.2)

The MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 requirements are assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT and to match the description rules stated in the RFP, and the current edition at kick-off governs. (S9.1)
"MHTC parameters" are assumed to be the property, right and deed data MoDOT supplies with its approved example LLDs, and the parameter set is confirmed with MoDOT at kick-off. (S9.1)
The proof-of-concept demonstration covers a set of properties drawn from MoDOT's approved example LLDs, sized to show variety of property type within the fixed price. (S23.1, S15.2)

Training is assumed to be a small number of instructor-led sessions for MoDOT ROW staff, delivered on-site or virtually with recordings, plus a standalone user manual, sized within the fixed price. (S24.1)
The literature review is assumed to be delivered as an annotated review with synthesis covering other state DOTs' AI/ML use for ROW purposes, with no fixed state list or time window imposed. (S20.1)

The named LLD development program is submitted with version, licence, hosting and security information at the same time as the name, and MoDOT Information Systems approval is assumed to be obtainable before the 4/25/2025 demonstration. (S22.1, S15.2)
Oracle 19C is treated as the default on-premise database, with SQL Server used only if MoDOT IS Data Service Management approves it. (S73.2)
The approved technology list in the RFP is treated as exhaustive, and any additional technology is cleared with the BRPT and IS management before use. (S73.1)
Python use is assumed to stay within ESRI scripts and small one-time uses, so no BRPT approval for large-scale Python use is priced. (S73.1)
The insurance limits are treated as firm contract requirements, with certificates furnished before contract signing rather than with the proposal. (S72.1)

The cost estimate is priced for the full contract term rather than an annual basis, and is submitted at the breakdown level of the Section (4) Price Page with a detailed budget developed after award. (S47.1, S45.1)
The 10% MBE and 5% WBE levels are treated as evaluated participation goals measured against total contract value, not as pass/fail requirements. (S55.1)

Confidential factual matters are assumed to be identified by MHTC marking at the time of supply, with notification of any third-party request made to MHTC's representative within one business day. (S66.1)

The Publications Guidelines, summary template, Proposal Submission Form, Price Page, cost estimate template, Standard Research Agreement and Exhibits A and B are obtained from MoDOT's information-researchers page and govern the corresponding deliverables. (S25.1, S26.1, S35.1, S45.1, S11.1, S59.1, S60.1)
The State of Missouri Accessibility Standard is assumed to be met by conforming to WCAG 2.1 AA plus the standard's published additions, obtained from the mo.gov link. (S73.2)

Qualification as a research organization is assumed to be demonstrated by past-three-years experience, named key personnel and three client references, with no additional registration or licence required beyond those the RFP states. (S8.1)
The 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central question deadline is treated as firm and as the only channel for clarification, so no late questions are relied on in the bid. (S12.1, S33.1)

Exhibits A and B not in the RFP, but affidavits are mandatory submission items. The RFP requires a sworn affidavit of lawful presence on Exhibit B and an E-Verify affidavit on Exhibit A, yet neither exhibit is included in the document. If the bidder cannot obtain the correct forms before 8/21/2024, the proposal is missing a mandatory submission item and risks being found non-responsive; if it improvises a form, the affidavit may be rejected. Either way the bid is at risk of disqualification or a post-award compliance failure. The affidavits are mandatory (R118, R119, R121) and the exhibits are confirmed absent from the PDF; the RFP does not say where they are obtained, so the outcome turns on facts the RFP leaves open.

EPG Section 236.4.6.2 not supplied, so the drafting rules the tool must encode are unverified. The RFP makes compliance with MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 a mandatory requirement for every description the tool drafts, but the section itself is not in the RFP. The proposed solution builds its requirements baseline from the RFP's summary of the rule and assumes the EPG text matches it. If the EPG contains additional or different requirements, the AI/ML engine, the acceptance checklist and the training manual all need rework after the demonstration, and the fixed price absorbs it. R011 is mandatory and the EPG is a confirmed missing document; the solution's own assumption that the EPG matches the RFP summary is an inference, not a fact the RFP settles.

MoDOT Information Systems approval gate before the 4/25/2025 demonstration. The solution may not proceed to the Task 3c proof of concept until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named LLD development program, and the demonstration is fixed at 4/25/2025. The RFP does not say what documentation the approval needs or how long it takes, and the solution assumes approval is obtainable in time. A slow or conditional review pushes the demonstration date, which is a contractual milestone, and the fixed price carries the idle time. R053 is a hard gate on a fixed milestone date and the approval criteria and turnaround are undefined; the solution's assumption that approval arrives before 4/25/2025 is unverified.

Fixed $175,000 cap against a build, train and report scope. The RFP caps the work at $175,000 not-to-exceed for a 15-month study that includes building a web application, an AI/ML drafting engine, a live demonstration, training, a maintained user manual and three report packages. The solution prices the full scope inside the cap and assumes the demonstration property set, training volume and literature review depth are all sized to fit. If any of those is larger than assumed, the bidder absorbs the overrun or cuts quality on a deliverable MoDOT evaluates. R042 is a hard cap and several scope drivers (training volume, number of demonstration properties, literature review depth) are undefined in the RFP; the solution's sizing is explicitly an assumption.

Contract term conflicts with the fixed milestone schedule. The RFP states a 15-month contract period but also fixes a 11/15/2024 kick-off and a 2/2/2026 contract end, which is roughly 14.5 months and does not reconcile with a 15-month term from the 11/1/2024 estimated start. The solution resolves the conflict by treating the fixed dates as governing. If MoDOT instead enforces the 15-month term from a later start, the final report and invoice dates move and the bidder's resourcing and billing plan are wrong. R016 and R041 conflict on their face; the solution's reading is an inference and the RFP does not say which controls.

Data Management Plan due date stated two different ways. The RFP fixes the DMP at 12/4/2024 in the milestone table and also requires it within two weeks of the kick-off meeting. With an 11/15/2024 kick-off the two dates coincide, but if the kick-off slips even a few days the two-week clock and the fixed date diverge, and the solution's assumption that 12/4/2024 satisfies both breaks. A late or contested DMP is an early contractual miss on a mandatory deliverable. R035 and R048 conflict; the solution's reconciliation depends on the kick-off date holding exactly, which the RFP does not guarantee.

Unreadable pages 19 and 20 may carry milestone or deliverable detail. Pages 19 and 20 of the RFP could not be parsed: each has only 19 words of text and an image covering 54% of the page. These pages sit in the section that defines the six tasks and their deliverables, so they may contain task descriptions, deliverable lists or acceptance criteria the bid does not see. If so, the proposal may omit a required deliverable or misprice a task. The pages are confirmed unreadable and fall in the task-definition section; whether they change the scope is unknown, which is exactly what makes the likelihood medium rather than low.

Price Page and cost estimate templates not supplied. The proposal must be submitted on the Section (4) Price Page with a cost estimate broken out by salaries, benefits, operating expense, F&A and miscellaneous, but neither the Price Page nor the cost estimate template is in the RFP. The solution assumes the breakdown level of the Price Page and defers a detailed budget to after award. If the actual template demands a different or finer breakdown, the pricing must be rebuilt late in the bid window, and a mis-formatted price page can make the proposal non-responsive. R094 and R095-R097 are mandatory and the templates are confirmed missing; the solution's assumption about the required breakdown level is untested.

Publication Guidelines and summary template unavailable, so report format is unconfirmed. The final report and 1-2 page research summary must follow the Publications Guidelines and summary template, and the final report must carry a completed Technical Report Documentation page, but the guidelines are referenced only as being on the website. The solution assumes it can obtain them and that they govern. If the format, page limits or documentation page differ from expectation, the report packages due 11/3/2025 and 1/1/2026 need rework close to the contract end. R059 and R064 are mandatory and the guidelines are a confirmed missing document; the risk is bounded because report formatting is rework rather than a design change.

Python and approved-technology constraints may not fit an AI/ML build. The solution commits to .NET with Python limited to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses, and treats the approved technology list as exhaustive. Most AI/ML tooling and model serving is Python-based, so if the engine needs substantial Python or a third-party library, the bidder must obtain BRPT and IS management approval or rebuild in C#. Either path costs schedule and money inside a fixed price, and the RFP does not define what counts as large-scale Python use. R139 and R137 are mandatory and the threshold for large-scale Python use is undefined; the solution's assumption that Python stays small is a design bet, not a settled fact.

WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard on a data-heavy drafting tool. The application must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, but the standard itself is referenced only by link and the solution assumes WCAG 2.1 AA plus published additions covers it. A drafting tool with generated text, review and edit workflows and map or ESRI components is hard to make fully accessible, and remediation discovered late in the build lands inside the fixed price and before the 4/25/2025 demonstration.
